ai.description: *Raorchestes garo* is a small frog (SVL 20–25 mm) with a brownish-grey dorsum and distinct dark interorbital markings. It is distinguished by a granular skin texture and a prominent white vocal sac.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Raorchestes garo* is best distinguished by its unique, prominent white spots on the dark-pigmented groin and hidden surfaces of the thighs, which are absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: *Raorchestes garo* inhabits evergreen and semi-evergreen forests in the Garo Hills, typically found perched on low vegetation at altitudes between 600 and 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Garo Hills bubble-nest frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small insects among the dense foliage of its forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes garo* exhibits direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. They breed during the monsoon (June–August), laying small clutches of eggs in leaf nests.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Raorchestes garo* is endemic to the Garo Hills of Meghalaya, India, where it inhabits mid-elevation evergreen forests within the Northeast Indian biogeographic zone.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Raorchestes garo* consists of a series of high-pitched, insect-like chirps, typically heard from vegetation in humid forest habitats.
